name: repository-level_change_propagation_analysis
mechanism: Static/dynamic change-impact analysis over a repository: changed entity -> affected dependents propagation.
evidence: Empirical change-impact study on real repositories.
metrics: Precision/recall of impact sets; cost = static/dynamic analysis time.
cost: No LLM cost; analysis tooling cost.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our dependency-graph impact selection (we rank candidate files from a parent-only graph).
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - change-impact analysis is a classical adjacent line; ours is intent-conditioned selection on real commits.
idea_to_test: Test: use change-propagation as a cheap non-LLM B3-graph alternative on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: RIPPLE refers to ripple-effect / change-propagation analysis; confirm exact paper/venue before citing.

name: Repository_Memory_(iterative_code_generation_memory)
mechanism: LLM agent with a 'repository memory' of generated code + clones; iterative retrieval over already-generated snippets during multi-file generation.
evidence: Pass@1 improvements on Codeforces; ablations on memory size/retrieval.
cost: Many LLM calls (10k+ per task in original study).
relation_to_us: Relates to our agentic/planner line: memory of previously seen code conditions later decisions, similar to iterative repo understanding.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - memory-conditioned generation is well-trodden; our contribution is cost-aware escalation, not memory per se.
idea_to_test: Test: contrast iterative memory retrieval vs our parent-snapshot BM25 over the candidate universe on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: Repository-level prompt generation (Reid & Neubig, ICML 2024) is the classic 'repo prompt' work; RepoCoder (ACL 2024) is the memory variant - disambiguate.

name: Adaptive_top-k_retrieval
mechanism: Retrieval-augmented systems that adapt the number of retrieved documents (top-k) per query instead of a fixed K.
evidence: Retrieval quality/cost trade-off analyses in RAG benchmarks.
relation_to_us: Directly motivates our 'K is an operating-point curve, not a final configuration' finding; K-selection policy is a candidate feature for omission-risk.
novelty_threat: LOW - adaptive-k is a known pattern; our K is per-method selection for localization, not retrieval depth.
idea_to_test: Test: fixed-K vs adaptive-K routing decision (risk-based) on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: Cross-domain inspiration: retrieval literature, not repository-localization-specific.

name: Graph-guided_localization_agent
mechanism: Graph-guided agent: dynamic AST+call graph, search/fix phases; localization file ranking as found_files.
evidence: We ran it (P5-B/P5-C): 10/10 held-out, 5 empty, 402 calls/32.8M tokens/$9.93 est.
datasets: djangoCMS real commits (our shared protocol); upstream SWE-bench-style.
relation_to_us: Our primary external comparator under the shared protocol.
novelty_threat: HIGH - the graph-guided agent is the natural 'strong' baseline for selective escalation; cost is the differentiator.
idea_to_test: Test: reuse as the expensive verifier in a future selective-escalation design (not now).

name: Graph-based_bug_localization
mechanism: Graph/network-based bug localization (e.g., suspiciousness propagation over call/co-change graphs).
evidence: Comparative localization studies on Defects4J-style data.
metrics: Rank@k, MAP, MRR; cost low (static graphs).
relation_to_us: Relates to our B3 Graph@K and the frozen parent-only dependency graph.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - graph localization is established; our twist is intent-conditioned cheap ranking + escalation, not raw graph mining.
idea_to_test: Test: compare graph-neighborhood features as omission-risk features (frontier size, reachable zone) on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: Verify exact paper; several graph-localization works exist under similar names.

name: Repository_graph_construction_for_LLM
mechanism: Automated repository graph construction (multi-quality AST + inheritance/function-call/README edges) used for LLM repo understanding and code retrieval.
evidence: Task-required code retrieval; LLM question answering over repos.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our dependency-graph construction; their graph is richer (AST-derived), ours is frozen parent-only AST graph.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - richer graph construction could improve our B3/Hybrid, but our cheap-seed finding suggests diminishing returns on the seed signal.
idea_to_test: Test: whether a richer graph (call+inheritance edges) changes B3/Hybrid on TRAIN/VALIDATION.

name: Agentless_localization_and_repair
mechanism: Decoupled two-phase pipeline: localize (file-level + line-level) then repair WITHOUT agentic search loops; each phase one LLM call.
evidence: SWE-bench Lite resolve rates at ~1/3 cost of agents.
relation_to_us: Strong evidence that 'localize first, no agent loop' is a competitive design - aligns with our sparse-first-pass + selective escalation.
novelty_threat: HIGH - 'agentless' localization-first is a direct conceptual competitor to graph/agent escalation being unnecessary for many tasks.
idea_to_test: Test: our BM25 first-pass + selective verification vs 'agentless-style' single-shot LLM localization on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: Preprint; later versions/venues - verify current status before citing.

name: Repository-level_coding_with_planning
mechanism: Plans the sequence of code edits across a repository: build/edit dependency plan, then per-file regeneration following the plan.
evidence: Edit-plan validity, codebuildability, edit overlap on real commits.
metrics: Plan validity; edit overlap; buildability; zero-shot plan completion.
relation_to_us: Directly comparable to our impact-planning (Full-v2/Sparse-v2) - both produce repository-level plans before edits.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - planning is a shared family; our contribution is the sparse representation + cost-aware escalation, not planning per se.
idea_to_test: Test: compare plan-edit-overlap semantics with our sparse plans (development evidence only).

name: RepoCoder_LLM_agent
mechanism: Clones-like retrieval into a repository memory; iteratively generates code conditioned on retrieved snippets.
evidence: Codeforces pass@1 gains; clone + memory ablations.
relation_to_us: Adjacent to RepoAgent/LocAgent line; memory-conditioned iteration vs our snapshot-conditioned cheap ranking.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - memory-conditioned iteration is established; not a direct threat to our cost-aware escalation.
idea_to_test: Test: none immediately; monitor as a future stronger LLM baseline under a fresh confirmatory protocol.

name: Autonomous_program_improvement
mechanism: Exploit-based repair: AST-level code search (API-based) + test-driven repair loop; bug localization via search.
evidence: SWE-bench resolve rates above many agents.
relation_to_us: Another strong agentic/repair comparator; localization is a component.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - repair-focused, our scope is localization-only (we do not claim regeneration).
idea_to_test: Test: none immediately (localization-only boundary); monitor for repair-benchmark positioning.

name: Zero-shot_repository-level_QA_via_repo_map
mechanism: ZeroRepO: build a repo map (repo map = hierarchical file/function manifest) then zero-shot retrieval + LLM QA over it.
evidence: Repo-level QA improvements vs long-context baselines.
metrics: QA accuracy; retrieval hit rate; token cost.
relation_to_us: Our candidate universe is essentially a repo map; the 'manifest first' design matches our public candidate-universe philosophy.
novelty_threat: MEDIUM - a manifest-based retrieval design is adjacent; our contribution is the selection-scoring + escalation budget.
idea_to_test: Test: candidate-universe-as-repo-map retrieval features (manifest density, module structure) as omission-risk features on TRAIN/VALIDATION.
notes: ZeroRepO; RPG may refer to a different 'RPG' (verify).

name: Agentic_or_adaptive_RAG
mechanism: Agentic/adaptive retrieval-augmented generation: the agent decides whether/when to retrieve and how many documents, based on query confidence.
relation_to_us: Conceptual template for our selective-escalation gate: low-risk accept, high-risk escalate.
novelty_threat: LOW-MEDIUM - adaptive retrieval is a known pattern; direct inspiration for the risk-gated escalation design.
idea_to_test: Test: risk-gate operating-point (AUROC/coverage curve) on TRAIN/VALIDATION for escalation decisions.
notes: AB-RAG abbreviation ambiguous - verify exact paper (Agentic RAG / Adaptive RAG).
